q: Synthetic homotopy theory in HoTT proves theorems about homotopy groups πₙ(Sⁿ) using only type-theoretic reasoning. The Freudenthal suspension theorem states:
opts: The suspension homomorphism E: πₙ(X) → πₙ₊₁(ΣX) is an isomorphism if X is (n−1)-connected and n ≥ 2·(connectivity of X)
exp: Freudenthal's theorem: if X is (k-1)-connected, the suspension E: πₙ(X) → πₙ₊₁(ΣX) is an isomorphism for n < 2k and surjection for n = 2k. In HoTT, this is proved using the 'join construction' and is one of the deepest results in synthetic homotopy theory.
